To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
retinol regulates RBP secretion in primary hepatocytes from rats with retinol deficiency.
the availability of retinaldehyde, the cellular form of retinol, specifically regulates the secretion rate of RBP by primary hepatocytes.

the metabolism of retinoic protein (RBP), the major transport protein for retinol, is regulated in cultured primary hepatocyte from retinol deficient rats, and that the effects seen are different than those seen in normal hepatocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the metabolism of RBP in cultured primary hepatocyte cells from normal (retionol‐adequate, RBP‐producing) rats and retinol‐ deficient (RBP‐accumulating) rats.
the regulation of the secretion of RRP by primary hepatocytes.
the role of retinol in the control of hepatic RBP synthesis and secretion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
retinol‐regulation of RBP production and secretion in hepatocytes is a specific and rapid effect that is seen only during retinol deficiency.

in retinol‐adequte hepatocytes, the availability of retinoic acids, not retinol, is the primary determinant of RBP secretion; whereas in retinol depletion, the availability of both retinol and retinoic acid is required for RBP synthesis and secretion.
in normal hepatocytes RBP synthesis is maintained by dexamethasome, and that in retinol‐replete hepatocytes retinol does little to stimulate RBP secretion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the regulation of RBP metabolism by retinol is a complex phenomenon that appears to be influenced by the nutritional status and by the presence or absence of glucocorticoids.
the secretion of RRP by hepatocytes is regulated by two mechanisms.
in retinol‐adequacy, retinoic acid is the active form of vitamin A that controls RBP synthesis and secretion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RBP secretion by hepatocytes is tightly regulated by the availability of retinoic within the cells.
retinol‐dependent and retinol‐independent mechanisms exist for the regulation of RBP metabolism in hepatocytes.
the regulation of RBP secretion by primary hepatocytes differs dramatically between normal (retinyl ester‐replete) cells and retinol‐ deficient cells, and is not mediated by the same mechanisms.
